narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your job, so the promotion decision has been denied at this time. This is a forecast based on patterns in employee data, not a certainty or a personal judgment.

The strongest driver was your total work experience: at 6–10 years, you fall into a group that is less common among employees predicted to stay (about 35%, compared with 50% in the 1–5 year group), and this raised the leave signal. Second was your tenure in your current organization at 1–5 years; although many stayers share this level, in your overall profile it also pushed the forecast toward leaving. Third was that you have other job opportunities. Only about 23% of employees predicted to stay reported having outside opportunities, so this was a meaningful signal that you may be considering leaving. Other profile factors such as low emotional commitment, no bonus, low job support, and feeling you did not get the deserved promotion reinforce the same direction, but the three above were the main drivers.

The organization should treat this as a retention conversation rather than a final judgment: clarify the promotion path, review pay and recognition, and discuss support and stability. You should also discuss what would make you stay and whether outside opportunities are influencing your plans.
